verdict: Reject as final banner; keep only as an external video generation experiment.

inspection.method: Visual inspection of decoded full scenes and 4x nearest-neighbor character crops at frames 0, 24, 48, 72, 96.
findings: Evan loses his original identity: by frame 24 the hair length and silhouette change, by frame 48 the body has taller adult proportions and long hair, and by frame 72 he turns frontward and resembles a different character.
Mir's horn angles, head shape, wing shape and size change substantially during the clip.
First/last frame conditioning brings the final pose closer to the initial reference but does not preserve identity through intermediate frames.
The stone path remains visually intact in the inspected samples; this is better than the procedural conveyor-like ground.
The canopy and flowers visibly change between samples, but sampled stills alone cannot establish natural wind motion or a smooth loop.
inspection.conclusion: The free external model is genuinely accessible and generated a video successfully, but this sample fails the essential original-character identity requirement. Do not describe it as a repaired or finished banner.
